doc.title: Cedar Walton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Why he will never retire
summary: Walton says playing for people is the best thing that could happen to an artist and compares himself to Ahmad Jamal who always says he is retiring.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: I know you like to get the checks. We talked about the surprises …
… you know, this has come up consistently as we've talked. Uh, but how important is it to just be on the bandstand. I know you like to get the gigs.
Yeah. Just uh … How important compared to what? Uh, getting the checks?
Compared to retiring, compared to not doing something.

This is not a sport, I mean. You can, you can play 'til you are uh in a wheelchair, which I think [sounds like: sun-ra] did. So I mean, uh, no, it uh, you don't, you don't uh retire. Well you could, I guess. Ahmad Jamal says that every year, says, "I'm retiring." Well he never does. He hasn't yet. Where to retire to? I mean, stop playin' the piano? Stop uh, uh going around having people listen to you and uh uh and your group play your music, or your versions of other people's music? That's a utopia to … in my view and the way I look at it. That's uh about the uh best uh thing that could happen to a person uh, uh, that's trying to be a creative artist.
